title: Grand Theft Auto 6 evreninde arka plan karakteri olmayacak
summary: Rockstar'ın aktardığına göre Grand Theft Auto 6 oyunundaki karakterler sıradan birer figüran değil; her birinin kendine ait yaşamı ve detaylı diyalogları bulunuyor.
body:
Polygon ve IGN'in aktardığına göre Rockstar, Grand Theft Auto 6 geliştirme sürecinde Florida'nın kültürünü ve insanlarını yakından incelemek için bölgeye ekipler gönderdi. Yazım direktörü James Horton, Love Magazine röportajında oyunda geleneksel anlamda boş bir arka plan bulunmadığını, her şeyin dikkat edilmesi gereken birer ön plan detayı olduğunu belirtti.

## Florida araştırması ve detaylı karakterler

Rockstar geliştirme ekibinden Aaron Garbut, projeye hazırlık aşamasında Miami ve çevre bölgelerde polisler ve çete üyeleriyle birlikte zaman geçirdiklerini, yerel halkla bir araya gelerek bölgenin zenginlik ve yoksulluk gibi tüm zıtlıklarını incelediklerini açıkladı. Bu derinlemesine araştırmanın oyun içindeki NPC'lerin yani yapay zeka karakterlerinin diyaloglarına, giyim tarzlarına ve saç stillerine yansıtıldığı ifade edildi.

## Modern dünyada Amerikan Rüyası

Oyunun ana karakterleri Jason ve Lucia, soygun dünyasına yeni adım atan ve tecrübesiz olan iki isim olarak öne çıkıyor. Stüdyo, hızla tüketilen internet trendlerinden kaçınarak hiciv unsurunu modern kültür ve komplo teorileri üzerine kurarken, hikayenin merkezinde ise günümüz şartlarında şekillenen Amerikan Rüyası yer alıyor.

**Neden önemli?** Rockstar, Grand Theft Auto 6 ile oyunculara yüzlerce saat keşfedebilecekleri, sıradan figüranlardan arındırılmış son derece canlı ve inandırıcı bir açık dünya sunmayı hedefliyor.

source_texts.title: GTA 6 Shows 'What the American Dream Looks Like Now' in a Game Without Background Characters
source_texts.summary: New interview reveals Grand Theft Auto 6 put hundreds of hours into NPC design and dialogue and tried its best to make an accurate-to-the-times GTA.
source_texts.text:
From what we've seen so far about Grand Theft Auto 6, it looks like one of the biggest open-world games in history. When developers have to create such sprawling virtual environments, there's a risk of them feeling empty or repetitive, but that doesn't seem to be the case with GTA 6. In a recent interview with Love Magazine, whose bits and screenshots have been shared by fans online, Rockstar revealed interesting details about the effort behind creating such a realistic world, with many stories and highly detailed characters. It also shared more about Lucia and Jason's hopes and dreams of fulfilling their American dream.
GTA 6 is a game without background
Rockstar is known for paying attention to details that are easy to overlook. That was evident in Red Dead Redemption 2, where the world felt truly alive, and it will be even more so in Grand Theft Auto 6. According to the interview with Love Magazine, Rockstar sent teams to various parts of Florida to study not only the locations and environments, but also its people and culture. This will be reflected in NPCs' conversations, clothing, and hairstyles.
Players will be able to spend hours observing these NPCs and still find new details and conversations to overhear. NPCs are meant to go beyond background characters that players can just run over without a second thought; they actually have a life of their own, and gamers can get to know them simply by listening to what they have to say. "In a world this dense, no one you meet is an extra," says the Instagram caption of the post advertising the new issue of the magazine.
"In a way, there's no 'background' in this game," writing director James Horton said in the Love interview. "There's just foreground you're not paying attention to right now."
With so much attention being put into NPCs' lives, hurting them might feel different from previous games, and that is why it is up to players to decide how Jason reacts to his own crimes and the situations happening around him. Rather than being a pair of tough, experienced criminals, he and Lucia are still new to the world of bank heists and drug deals. They must be careful navigating it so they don't fly too close to the sun and get burned because of their inexperience.
Jason is shaping up to be a very relatable character that players can connect with, especially considering that they significantly influence who he becomes. However, this will change Jason's reputation, and others will react differently to him, whether positively or negatively.
GTA 6 will still be about the American Dream
While you might not see short-lived internet trends and obsessions like Labubus or brainrot, as they'd easily make the game feel dated, Grand Theft Auto 6 has found other ways to capture the current zeitgeist. Rockstar confirms that GTA 6 is still very much about chasing the American dream, but in this day and age.
"Some would say the American Dream collapsed a long time ago," Robert Humphries, senior vice president of narrative, said in the Love interview. "Maybe the American Dream is more modest now. It's a house for your family and your loans paid off instead of wild success — but maybe today, that is just as out of reach for the average person."
When ordering Love Magazine issue 27, fans can choose from several cover variants. As expected, the Love Magazine with the cover art featuring Jason and Lucia quickly sold out. Nevertheless, the contents are the same regardless of the cover, and the issue will be out on Oct. 5.

source_texts.title: Rockstar Traveled Across Florida With Gang Members and Cops for GTA 6 Research
source_texts.summary: Rockstar has discussed travelling across Florida with gang members and cops for GTA 6 research, and hovering in a helicopter above a Beyonce concert.
source_texts.text:
Love Magazine recently got an exclusive interview with Rockstar Games ahead of GTA 6’s release next month. While the interview focuses primarily on the love story between dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, there’s some interesting insight into the studio’s process for creating the most impressive virtual worlds ever made.
For its rendition of Florida, team members spent lots of time embedding with the culture and exploring the landscape of Miami and its surrounding areas. These research trips start small as the leads scout out the most interesting locations and stories, and more team members come on subsequent trips to dive deeper into the culture, stories, and people.
“Every game we make starts with research trips. It’s where to get to explore both the place and our ideas as a group,” head of development Aaron Garbut said. “To begin, a small group of us spent some time traveling from Miami through some of the surrounding towns and through the Florida Keys down to Key West. This is one of the best parts of the entire project: a car full of friends, driving for days on end, talking about what we want to make and being immersed in the locations and our ideas.”
Garbut takes a camera and a phone and records everything that happens. During one shoot, a handful of Rockstar devs spent the day flying low and fast over mangrove inlets in the everglades, before ending the day hovering over a stadium with a live Beyonce concert playing. “I think we made the local news that day,” Garbut said.
“We do go in-depth, we hang with locals and we hear lots of stories and learn as much as we can. We travel around with cops and with gang members. Everyone is lovely. Some people are equally scary. We experience the underside as well; although the people who showed us around were among the nicest we’ve met, the stories, the places, the details could be terrifying. We try to build a world that is believable and varied, with depth, so that is the research we need.
“Miami itself is really those extremes — lovely people, incredible wealth, incredible poverty, excess, craziness, the hustle, and showing it all off. That’s our research trips — experiencing those extremes so that we can bring them into our world, and it all finds its way into the game in surprising ways.”
Some of those surprising ways could be pedestrian dialogue or radio shows and advertisements, which Rockstar said it doesn’t treat as secondary content. Everything is important when creating a world you want players to spend hundreds of hours exploring.
Rockstar’s approach to a GTA game set in the modern day is to deliberately avoid recreating real-world viral moments, since long development timelines mean these kinds of references can date a game — ask Borderlands. Instead, GTA 6’s satire focuses on modern culture, conspiracy theories, and “the strange ways people react to events.”
Last week, local team the Miami Heat announced a special match, during which the Heat will wear a GTA 6 uniform in a themed arena. We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games, our GTA 6 preview, and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor.
